info.name: Fraud Detection API
info.description:
Comprehensive Postman collection for the Twenty9ine Fraud Detection Service.

**Folder run order**

1. **Authentication** — issue tokens for `detector`, `analyst`, `admin`, and the `fraud-detection-kafka` service client. Stores tokens in environment variables (`detectorToken`, `analystToken`, `adminToken`, `kafkaToken`, `refreshToken`). **Run this folder first** — every other folder depends on those variables.
2. **Authorization Matrix** — exhaustively asserts the 401/403/200 grid for every `/fraud/**` endpoint × {no token, detector, analyst, admin}.
3. **Risk Assessment Scenarios** — the eight scenarios suggested in the README (Low/Medium/High/Critical, Mockoon-driven account integration, Get-by-ID round-trip, search by risk levels, search by date range).
4. **Validation & Errors** — documented 400/404 paths (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `INVALID_RISK_LEVEL`, `RISK_ASSESSMENT_NOT_FOUND`).
5. **Actuator** — public probes (`/health`, `/info`) and the auth-protected operational endpoints; also asserts that `/actuator/{prometheus,heapdump,caches}` are *not* wired up in this build.

Every request includes `pm.test(...)` assertions. Use the *Local* environment shipped alongside this file (`Fraud-Detection-Local.postman_environment.json`).

Credentials and secrets in the environment file are the literal values from `docker-compose/keycloak-config/fraud-detection-realm.json` for **local development only**.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Token grants for each Keycloak client + the documented negative cases.

request.description: Issues a JWT for `detector` (granted realm role `fraud_detector` → resource_access role `fraud:detect` → SCOPE_fraud:detect → `POST /fraud/assessments` only). Stores the token as `{{detectorToken}}` and the refresh token as `{{refreshToken}}`.
Issues a JWT for `analyst` (realm role `fraud_analyst` → SCOPE_fraud:read → `GET /fraud/assessments**` only). Stored as `{{analystToken}}`.
Issues a JWT for `admin` (composite role `fraud_admin` → both `fraud:detect` and `fraud:read`). Stored as `{{adminToken}}`.

Service-account token used by Kafka producers/consumers for SASL/OAUTHBEARER. Lives 1 hour; the kafka client does not issue refresh tokens. The token's audience is `account` (NOT `fraud-detection-service`), so it cannot be used to call `/fraud/**` endpoints — see the negative test below.

Exchanges the stored refresh token for a fresh access token. Requires `Get Token — detector` (or one of the other web-client grants) to have populated `{{refreshToken}}` first. Updates `{{detectorToken}}` and `{{refreshToken}}` with the new pair.
Sanity check that Keycloak rejects a wrong client secret with `unauthorized_client`. This is the failure the original README's placeholder secret produced.

exec: pm.test('error_description mentions direct access grants', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error_description).to.include('direct access grants'));

request.description: `fraud-detection-service` is a resource server — `directAccessGrantsEnabled=false`. Verifies Keycloak refuses the password grant with `unauthorized_client: Client not allowed for direct access grants`.

exec: pm.test('Status 401 (Keycloak returns 401 for this rejection, vs 400 for password-grant rejection)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

request.description: `fraud-detection-service` also has `serviceAccountsEnabled=false`, so client_credentials is also rejected: `Client not enabled to retrieve service account`.

item.name: Authorization Matrix
item.description: Asserts the 401/403/200 grid for every `/fraud/**` endpoint × {no token, detector, analyst, admin}. Run **Authentication** first.

exec: pm.test('riskScore is in 0..100', () => { const s = json.riskScore; pm.expect(s).to.be.at.least(0); pm.expect(s).to.be.at.most(100); });

request.description: Uses `lastAssessmentTransactionId` populated by the Risk Assessment Scenarios folder. If you run this folder before that one, expect 404 (still proves authorization passes through to the controller).

exec: pm.test('Status 401 (audience does not include fraud-detection-service)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

request.description: The kafka client_credentials token's audience is `account` only; the resource server's AudienceValidator rejects it for `/fraud/**`.

item.name: Risk Assessment Scenarios
item.description: The eight scenarios suggested in the README. Most use `detector` for POST and the chained Get-by-ID uses `analyst`.

request.description: Same-city transaction with a small amount. Expect LOW risk → ALLOW.

exec: pm.test('Decision is ALLOW or CHALLENGE (depending on rules)', () => pm.expect(json.decision).to.be.oneOf(['ALLOW','CHALLENGE','REVIEW','BLOCK']));

request.description: Large-amount purchase that exercises the LARGE_AMOUNT Drools rule. Exact decision depends on rule weights and ML availability.
Re-run this request several times in quick succession against the same `{{velocityAccount}}` to trigger the VELOCITY_5MIN rule. Risk level rises with each repeat.

Account `ACC-IMPOSSIBLE-001`'s last-known location (per Mockoon) is Johannesburg, ZA. Posting a Tokyo-located transaction with `transactionTimestamp = now` requires >965 km/h — triggering the IMPOSSIBLE_TRAVEL rule.
Calls `AccountServiceRestAdapter` against the Mockoon mock at :3001. The transaction location is close to the account's home, so distance-based risk stays low.

exec: pm.test('Status 200 (assumes scenario 1 or 5 ran first)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Round-trip read of the most-recently-created assessment. Run after scenario 1 or 5.

exec: pm.test('Every result is HIGH or CRITICAL', () => json.content.forEach(a => pm.expect(['HIGH','CRITICAL']).to.include(a.transactionRiskLevel)));
// Default to 1 day ago if user hasn't overridden the variable.

request.description: `WITHDRAWAL` is not a valid TransactionType — the real value is `ATM_WITHDRAWAL`.

item.name: Actuator
item.description: Health/info are public; everything else requires a valid JWT. The READMEs note that prometheus/heapdump/caches are NOT actually wired up — the last three requests assert the resulting 5xx.

exec: pm.test('Not exposed (5xx via global handler, or 404)', () => pm.expect([404, 500]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: Documented as NOT wired up. Add `io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus` and include `prometheus` in `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include` to enable.
